summary: Ventura County AWS post built 1942-43 for aircraft spotting and fire detection; the register lists it as gone with no removal date.

facts.design: standard AWS post structure with a ground cabin and cupola
facts.status_note: Register list shows Gone; detail page gives removal as unknown; no source describes what remains

staffing.status: built, provisioned and staffed by the US Forest Service for the Aircraft Warning Service; fire detection may have continued after WWII

facts.agency: US Forest Service - Los Padres National Forest

events.note: Built 1942-43 per the register's Built field; description says constructed in 1942/43
Registered April 16, 2020; nominated by Brad Eells

evidence.supports: built 1942-43 as a standard AWS post with ground cabin and cupola
evidence.quote: A standard AWS post structure with a ground cabin and cupola were constructed in 1942/43

evidence.supports: dual purpose: enemy aircraft spotting and fire detection
evidence.quote: The Mount Pinos structure was a dual purpose site, used for enemy aircraft spotting and fire detection

evidence.supports: elevation 8,847 ft in Los Padres National Forest, Ventura County
Forest Service built, provisioned and staffed the posts
evidence.quote: The US Forest Service built, provisioned and staffed these posts.

evidence.supports: Army reimbursed the Forest Service for all costs
evidence.quote: The US Army reimbursed the US Forest Service for all costs.

evidence.supports: operators reported aircraft and fires to USFS dispatch; aircraft information relayed to the Army
evidence.quote: Operators were expected to report all aircraft activities and report all fires and smokes to USFS dispatch.

evidence.supports: forest fire detection as early as 1927 per newspapers; pre-WWII structure unknown
evidence.quote: Forest fire detection was occurring as early as 1927 according to newspaper reports. It is unknown if any structure was built prior to WWII.

evidence.supports: fire detection may have continued after WWII; removal date unknown
evidence.quote: Fire detection may have continued after WWII. Building removal date is unknown.

evidence.supports: registered April 16, 2020; nominated by Brad Eells
location: Los Padres National Forest, Ventura County
aircraft information relayed to the Army
evidence.quote: Aircraft information was then relayed to the Army.

evidence.supports: AWS expanded: the register titles the site an Aircraft Warning Service site
evidence.quote: Mount Pinos - Aircraft Warning Service Site

evidence.supports: Peakbagging describes the structure as the airplane spotting structure on Mount Pinos during WWII
evidence.quote: This is the airplane spotting structure that was on Mount Pinos during World War II.

evidence.supports: may also have served as a fire lookout for some years
evidence.quote: This may have also been used as a fire lookout for some years.

evidence.supports: list page records the Mount Pinos AWS site as Gone
evidence.quote: Pinos, Mount AWS Ventura 34.81286 -119.14538 AWS Gone

sources.title: Mount Pinos, Airplane Spotting Station, California

corrections.why: The register's Built field reads 1942-43 and its description says the structure was constructed in 1942/43.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The list page marks the site Gone, but the detail page gives removal as unknown. The story uses the list status and says the removal date is unknown.

notes_for_editor: Only the register detail page, the register list and one PeakBagging page were read; no Forest Service record was found. The Wikipedia article for Mount Pinos does not mention the post. The PeakBagging page credits a photo to Fred Johnson dated May 15, 1943, but it gives no image URL, so no photo entry was added. Grokipedia was not used.
